records.title: Packet resolved transfer system
records.label: strengthened:definition:1
records.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Packet resolved transfer system]
A packet resolved transfer system is a triple
\[
(X,A,\Pcal)
\]
consisting of a Banach state space, a bounded generator, and a finite packet system. A marked transfer system also includes an initial state or source $s\in X$. The topology and all limiting operations are supplied by the ambient Banach space structure.
\end{definition}
records.review_note: Context, definition, example, or scope remark read; not counted as a proved result.

records.title: Packet blocks
records.label: strengthened:definition:2
records.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Packet blocks]
For \(B\in\mathcal B(X)\), define
\[
B_{\beta\alpha}=P_\beta BP_\alpha.
\]
If \(A\in\mathcal B(X)\) and \(T(t)=\e^{tA}\), write
\[
T_{\beta\alpha}(t)=P_\beta T(t)P_\alpha.
\]
\end{definition}
records.review_note: Context, definition, example, or scope remark read; not counted as a proved result.

records.title: Semigroup and packet convolution
records.label: thm:packet_convolution
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Semigroup and packet convolution]\label{thm:packet_convolution}
For every bounded operator \(A\), the family \(T(t)=\e^{tA}\) is a uniformly continuous group and
\[
T(s+t)=T(s)T(t).
\]
For every \(\alpha,\beta\in I\),
\[
T_{\beta\alpha}(s+t)
=
\sum_{\gamma\in I}
T_{\beta\gamma}(s)T_{\gamma\alpha}(t).
\]
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Norm absolutely convergent exponential Cauchy product; finite resolution of identity inserted. The group parameter is real; uniform continuity is the conventional norm-continuity-at-zero property.

records.title: Block differential system
records.label: prop:block_differential
records.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Block differential system]\label{prop:block_differential}
The packet blocks are differentiable in operator norm and satisfy
\[
\frac{\dd}{\dd t}T_{\beta\alpha}(t)
=
\sum_{\gamma\in I}
A_{\beta\gamma}T_{\gamma\alpha}(t)
=
\sum_{\gamma\in I}
T_{\beta\gamma}(t)A_{\gamma\alpha}.
\]
Their initial values are
\[
T_{\beta\alpha}(0)=\delta_{\beta\alpha}P_\alpha.
\]
\end{proposition}
records.review_note: Differentiate norm series; both block products follow by the finite resolution. Initial off-diagonal blocks vanish.

records.title: Laplace resolvent and packet transform
records.label: thm:laplace_packet_resolvent
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Laplace resolvent and packet transform]\label{thm:laplace_packet_resolvent}
Let \(A\in\mathcal B(X)\), let \(T(t)=\e^{tA}\), and let
\[
\operatorname{Re}z>\norm A.
\]
Then the Bochner integral converges in operator norm and
\[
(zI-A)^{-1}
=
\int_0^\infty \e^{-zt}T(t)\dd t.
\]
For every pair of packets,
\[
P_\beta(zI-A)^{-1}P_\alpha
=
\int_0^\infty
\e^{-zt}T_{\beta\alpha}(t)\dd t.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
The estimate \(\norm{T(t)}\leq\e^{t\norm A}\) gives absolute convergence of the operator valued integral. Let
\[
R(z)=\int_0^\infty\e^{-zt}T(t)\dd t.
\]
Since \(T'(t)=AT(t)=T(t)A\), integration by parts gives
\[
(zI-A)R(z)
=
-\int_0^\infty
\frac{\dd}{\dd t}
\bigl(\e^{-zt}T(t)\bigr)
\dd t
=I.
\]
The same calculation on the other side gives
\(
R(z)(zI-A)=I
\).
Multiplication by \(P_\beta\) and \(P_\alpha\) may be passed under the norm convergent integral, which gives the packet formula.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Re z > ||A|| ensures integrability and decay. Integration of the norm derivative gives both inverse identities, then bounded multiplication commutes with Bochner integration.

records.title: Resolvent expansion over packet paths
records.label: cor:resolvent_packet_paths
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Resolvent expansion over packet paths]\label{cor:resolvent_packet_paths}
With \(A=D+N\) as in the directed path decomposition, let
\[
R_D(z)=(zI-D)^{-1}.
\]
If
\[
\norm{R_D(z)N}<1,
\]
then
\[
(zI-A)^{-1}
=
\sum_{m=0}^\infty
\bigl(R_D(z)N\bigr)^mR_D(z).
\]
After multiplication by \(P_\beta\) and \(P_\alpha\), the term of order \(m\) is a sum over directed packet paths of length \(m\) from \(\alpha\) to \(\beta\).
\end{corollary}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Factor
\[
zI-A=(zI-D)(I-R_D(z)N)
\]
and expand the second inverse by its norm convergent Neumann series. The diagonal resolvent preserves each packet and every factor \(N\) changes the packet along an active transfer edge.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Order checked: zI-A=(zI-D)(I-R_D N), so inverse is (I-R_D N)^(-1)R_D. The condition presupposes z in the resolvent set of D.

records.title: Reducing packet criterion
records.label: thm:reducing_packets
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
The first two conditions are equivalent because the packet resolution gives
\[
AP_\alpha=\sum_\beta A_{\beta\alpha},
\qquad
P_\alpha A=\sum_\gamma A_{\alpha\gamma}.
\]
A block diagonal generator has block diagonal powers, so the second condition implies the third. Differentiating the off diagonal blocks at zero proves the converse. The equivalence with invariance follows from the definition of the blocks. The final identity follows by restricting the exponential series.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Commutation iff off-diagonal generator blocks vanish; differentiation at zero supplies necessity. All packets invariant gives block diagonal powers. Restrictions are operators on packet ranges.

records.title: Dyson expansion over packet paths
records.label: thm:dyson_paths
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Write the variation of constants identity
\[
\e^{tA}
=
\e^{tD}
+
\int_0^t\e^{(t-s)D}N\e^{sA}\dd s.
\]
Iterating the identity gives the displayed series. The norm of the term of order \(m\) is at most
\[
\e^{t\norm D}\frac{(t\norm N)^m}{m!}.
\]
The majorant is summable. Inserting the packet resolution around every factor \(N\) leaves only products whose consecutive packet labels are joined by nonzero transfer blocks.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Variation of constants iterated in correct order. Simplex volume t^m/m! and norm bound exp(t||D||)||N||^m yield absolute convergence.

records.title: Termination on an acyclic transfer graph
records.label: cor:acyclic_termination
records.review_note: Each surviving term induces m edges; no path exceeds longest acyclic path. Length-zero paths supply diagonal terms.

records.title: Duhamel defect identity
records.label: thm:duhamel_defect
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Duhamel defect identity]\label{thm:duhamel_defect}
For every \(t\geq0\),
\[
\mathfrak D(t)
=
\int_0^t
\e^{(t-s)A_c}\Delta\e^{sA_f}
\dd s.
\]
If
\[
\norm{\e^{tA_f}}\leq M_f\e^{\omega_f t},
\qquad
\norm{\e^{tA_c}}\leq M_c\e^{\omega_c t},
\]
then
\[
\norm{\mathfrak D(t)}
\leq
M_fM_c\norm\Delta
\int_0^t
\e^{\omega_c(t-s)+\omega_fs}
\dd s.
\]
For contraction semigroups,
\[
\norm{\mathfrak D(t)}\leq t\norm\Delta.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
For fixed \(t\), set
\[
F(s)=\e^{(t-s)A_c}C\e^{sA_f}.
\]
Then
\[
F'(s)=\e^{(t-s)A_c}\Delta\e^{sA_f}.
\]
Integrating from zero to \(t\) gives the identity. The estimates follow by taking norms under the integral.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Derivative of exp((t-s)A_c) C exp(sA_f) gives +Delta with correct types; both endpoint terms and growth factors checked.

records.title: Infinitesimal recovery of the defect
records.label: prop:infinitesimal_defect
records.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Infinitesimal recovery of the defect]\label{prop:infinitesimal_defect}
The generator defect is the first order semigroup defect:
\[
\lim_{t\to0}
\frac{\mathfrak D(t)}{t}
=
\Delta
\]
in operator norm. Consequently,
\[
C\e^{tA_f}=\e^{tA_c}C
\quad\hbox{for every }t
\]
if and only if \(CA_f=A_cC\).
\end{proposition}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
The operator norm expansions
\[
\e^{tA_f}=I+tA_f+o(t),
\qquad
\e^{tA_c}=I+tA_c+o(t)
\]
give the limit. The equivalence follows from this limit and \cref{thm:duhamel_defect}.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Norm Taylor expansion yields Delta; converse follows from Duhamel. No unbounded-generator extension is inferred.

records.title: Resolvent defect identity
records.label: thm:resolvent_defect
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Resolvent defect identity]\label{thm:resolvent_defect}
Let \(z\) belong to the resolvent sets of \(A_f\) and \(A_c\). With
\[
R_f(z)=(zI-A_f)^{-1},
\qquad
R_c(z)=(zI-A_c)^{-1},
\]
one has
\[
CR_f(z)-R_c(z)C
=
R_c(z)\Delta R_f(z).
\]
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Left multiplication by zI-A_c and right multiplication by zI-A_f reduce both sides to Delta. Rectangular C permitted.

records.title: Exact naturality
records.label: cor:exact_naturality
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Exact naturality]\label{cor:exact_naturality}
If \(CA_f=A_cC\), then
\[
Cg(A_f)=g(A_c)C
\]
for every holomorphic function covered by \cref{thm:holomorphic_defect}. The conclusion includes exponentials, resolvents, and polynomials.
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Set Delta=0 in the corrected admissible-contour formula; exponentials and polynomials are entire and resolvents use holomorphic neighborhoods avoiding their pole.

records.title: Exact projective limit semigroup
records.label: thm:exact_projective_limit
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Exact projective limit semigroup]\label{thm:exact_projective_limit}
For each \(\ell\), let \(T_\ell(t)\) be a strongly continuous semigroup on \(X_\ell\). Assume
\[
C_\ell T_{\ell+1}(t)=T_\ell(t)C_\ell
\]
for every \(\ell\) and \(t\geq0\), and assume the uniform bound
\[
\sup_\ell\norm{T_\ell(t)}\leq M\e^{\omega t}.
\]
Define
\[
T_\infty(t)(x_\ell)_\ell
=
(T_\ell(t)x_\ell)_\ell.
\]
Then \(T_\infty(t)\) is a bounded semigroup on \(X_\infty\). It is strongly continuous if
\[
\lim_{t\downarrow0}
\sup_\ell
\norm{T_\ell(t)x_\ell-x_\ell}=0
\]
for every \((x_\ell)_\ell\in X_\infty\).

If \(T_\ell(t)=\e^{tA_\ell}\), the generators are bounded, and
\[
\sup_\ell\norm{A_\ell}<\infty,
\qquad
C_\ell A_{\ell+1}=A_\ell C_\ell,
\]
then the continuity condition holds and
\[
A_\infty(x_\ell)_\ell=(A_\ell x_\ell)_\ell
\]
is the bounded generator of \(T_\infty\).
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Exact intertwining shows that \((T_\ell(t)x_\ell)_\ell\) remains compatible. The uniform growth bound makes the coordinatewise operator bounded on the supremum norm. The semigroup law holds in every coordinate. The stated continuity condition is exactly strong continuity in the supremum norm.

For bounded generators with common bound \(M_A\),
\[
\sup_\ell
\norm{(\e^{tA_\ell}-I)x_\ell}
\leq
(\e^{tM_A}-1)\sup_\ell\norm{x_\ell}.
\]
This tends to zero with \(t\). Exact generator intertwining makes \((A_\ell x_\ell)_\ell\) compatible, and coordinatewise differentiation identifies the generator.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Growth bound preserves bounded coordinates; compatibility preserves inverse limit. Strong continuity needs the stated uniform-in-level condition. Uniformly bounded compatible generators satisfy it and define a bounded generator.

records.title: Reconstructed fine evolution
records.label: strengthened:definition:18
records.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Reconstructed fine evolution]
For a semigroup \(T_n(t)\) on \(X_n\), define the evolution seen from level \(m\) by
\[
U_{m,n}(t)=C_{m,n}T_n(t)R_{n,m}.
\]
\end{definition}

records.title: Weighted summable defect completion
records.label: thm:summable_defect_completion
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Weighted summable defect completion]\label{thm:summable_defect_completion}
Define the adjacent semigroup defect
\[
E_n(t)=C_nT_{n+1}(t)-T_n(t)C_n.
\]
Fix a coarse level \(m\) and a time horizon \(T>0\). For \(n\geq m\), set
\[
w_{m,n}
=
\norm{C_{m,n}}\,
\norm{R_nR_{n,m}}.
\]
If
\[
\sum_{n=m}^{\infty}
w_{m,n}
\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\norm{E_n(t)}<\infty,
\]
then \(U_{m,n}(t)\) converges in operator norm uniformly for \(0\leq t\leq T\). Its limit is denoted by \(U_m(t)\), and
\[
\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}
\norm{U_m(t)-U_{m,n}(t)}
\leq
\sum_{j=n}^{\infty}w_{m,j}
\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\norm{E_j(t)}.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Exact difference is C_(m,n) E_n R_n R_(n,m). Weighted summability yields uniform operator-norm Cauchy convergence and tail bound. It does not prove a semigroup law.

records.title: Contractive summable defect completion
records.label: cor:contractive_defect_completion
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Contractive summable defect completion]\label{cor:contractive_defect_completion}
Assume
\[
\norm{C_\ell}\leq1,
\qquad
\norm{R_\ell}\leq1,
\qquad
\norm{T_\ell(t)}\leq1
\]
for every \(\ell\) and \(t\geq0\). If
\[
\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}
\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\norm{E_\ell(t)}<\infty,
\]
then the conclusion of \cref{thm:summable_defect_completion} holds, and
\[
\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}
\norm{U_m(t)-U_{m,n}(t)}
\leq
\sum_{\ell=n}^{\infty}
\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\norm{E_\ell(t)}.
\]
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Every reconstruction/coarsening product has norm at most one, so each weight is at most one.

records.title: Generator defect criterion
records.label: cor:generator_defect_completion
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Generator defect criterion]\label{cor:generator_defect_completion}
Assume
\[
\norm{C_\ell}\leq1,
\qquad
\norm{R_\ell}\leq1,
\]
and suppose \(T_\ell(t)=\e^{tA_\ell}\) are contraction semigroups with bounded generators. Set
\[
\Delta_\ell=C_\ell A_{\ell+1}-A_\ell C_\ell.
\]
If
\[
\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}\norm{\Delta_\ell}<\infty,
\]
then the conclusion of \cref{cor:contractive_defect_completion} holds on every bounded time interval, and
\[
\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}
\norm{U_m(t)-U_{m,n}(t)}
\leq
T\sum_{\ell=n}^{\infty}\norm{\Delta_\ell}.
\]
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Adjacent contraction Duhamel estimate is t||Delta_n||; sum gives T times tail on [0,T]. No uniform generator-norm bound is required for this estimate.

records.title: Asymptotic closure criterion
records.label: thm:asymptotic_closure

records.title: Summable defects do not force a semigroup limit
records.label: ex:summable_not_semigroup
records.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[Summable defects do not force a semigroup limit]\label{ex:summable_not_semigroup}
Let \(X_0=\RR\) and let \(X_n=\RR^2\) for every \(n\geq1\). Set
\[
C_0(x,y)=x,
\qquad
R_0x=(x,0),
\]
and use identity connecting maps and reconstructions above level one. Let \(T_0(t)=I\) and let every higher level carry the rotation group
\[
T_n(t)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos t&-\sin t\\
\sin t&\cos t
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Only the first adjacent defect is nonzero, so every defect sum is finite. Yet for \(n\geq1\),
\[
U_{0,n}(t)=C_0T_n(t)R_0=\cos t.
\]
The limiting family is not a semigroup because in general
\[
\cos(s+t)\neq\cos s\cos t.
\]
The failure is exactly the excursion from the reconstructed line into its orthogonal complement between two time steps.
\end{example}
records.review_note: Context, definition, example, or scope remark read; not counted as a proved result.

records.title: Range leakage criterion
records.label: prop:range_leakage
records.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Range leakage criterion]\label{prop:range_leakage}
Under the contractive assumptions of \cref{cor:contractive_defect_completion}, define
\[
\eta_{m,n}(T)
=
\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}
\norm{(I-P_{m,n})T_n(t)R_{n,m}}.
\]
Then
\[
\rho_{m,n}(T)\leq\eta_{m,n}(T).
\]
Consequently, \(\eta_{m,n}(T)\to0\) for every \(T>0\) is sufficient for the limiting family \(U_m\) to satisfy the semigroup law.
\end{proposition}
records.review_note: Drop contraction factors C_(m,n)T_n(s). Vanishing reconstructed-range leakage implies vanishing closure defect.

records.title: Generator control of range leakage
records.label: thm:generator_range_leakage
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
For \(x\in PX\), write
\[
p(t)=PT(t)x,
\qquad
q(t)=QT(t)x.
\]
The hidden component satisfies
\[
q'(t)=QAQq(t)+QAPp(t),
\qquad
q(0)=0.
\]
Variation of constants gives
\[
q(t)=
\int_0^t
\e^{(t-s)(QAQ)|_{QX}}
QAPp(s)
\dd s.
\]
Since
\(
\norm{p(s)}\leq\norm P\norm{T(s)}\norm x
\)
and \(x=Px\), the first estimate follows. The contraction case is immediate.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Solve hidden equation driven by retained component. Two factors ||P|| arise when input x=P y and retained part is bounded. Orthogonal case has ||P||≤1. Bounded A scope must stay explicit.

records.title: A usable closure condition for refinement towers
records.label: cor:generator_closure_tower
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
A bounded generator of a contraction semigroup on a Hilbert space is dissipative. If \(Q_{m,n}=I-P_{m,n}\) and \(y\in Q_{m,n}X_n\), then
\[
\operatorname{Re}\ip{Q_{m,n}A_nQ_{m,n}y}{y}
=
\operatorname{Re}\ip{A_ny}{y}
\leq0.
\]
Hence the compressed hidden semigroup is contractive. Apply \cref{thm:generator_range_leakage} to \(P_{m,n}\). Since \(P_{m,n}R_{n,m}=R_{n,m}\),
\[
\eta_{m,n}(T)
\leq
T\norm{(I-P_{m,n})A_nP_{m,n}}
\norm{R_{n,m}}.
\]
The right side tends to zero. Use \cref{prop:range_leakage}.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Orthogonal compression preserves dissipativity, hence its bounded exponential is contractive by differentiating squared norm. ||R_(n,m)||≤1 then controls leakage.

records.title: Canonical lumping obstruction
records.label: strengthened:definition:29
records.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Canonical lumping obstruction]
For a linear fine transition operator \(K\), define
\[
\Ob_C(K)
=
(CK)|_{\Ker C}
\in
\mathcal B(\Ker C,\RR^m).
\]
\end{definition}
records.review_note: Context, definition, example, or scope remark read; not counted as a proved result.

records.title: Descent through an aggregation map
records.label: thm:canonical_lumping_obstruction
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Descent through an aggregation map]\label{thm:canonical_lumping_obstruction}
Let \(C:X_f\to X_c\) be a surjective linear map between finite dimensional spaces. A unique operator \(\overline K:X_c\to X_c\) satisfying
\[
CK=\overline KC
\]
exists if and only if
\[
\Ob_C(K)=0.
\]
For any right inverse \(R\) of \(C\), the only possible coarse operator is
\[
\overline K=CKR,
\]
and
\[
CK-\overline KC
=
CK(I-RC).
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
If \(CK=\overline KC\), then \(CK\) vanishes on \(\Ker C\). Conversely, suppose the obstruction vanishes and define
\[
\overline K(Cx)=CKx.
\]
If \(Cx=Cy\), then \(x-y\in\Ker C\), so the value does not depend on the representative. Surjectivity defines \(\overline K\) on all of \(X_c\), and the intertwining relation follows from the definition. It also gives uniqueness. If \(R\) is a right inverse, then
\[
\overline K=\overline KCR=CKR.
\]
Substitution gives the defect identity.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Surjective quotient descent exists iff CK vanishes on ker C. Formula CKR is independent of R only when obstruction vanishes; raw defect formula is valid for arbitrary R.

records.title: Coordinate form of the lumping obstruction
records.label: cor:lumping_obstruction_coordinates
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Coordinate form of the lumping obstruction]\label{cor:lumping_obstruction_coordinates}
For the partition aggregation above, \(\Ker C\) is spanned by differences \(e_i-e_j\) with \(i\) and \(j\) in one source block. Also,
\[
\Ob_C(K)(e_i-e_j)
=
\left(
\sum_{r\in B_\alpha}(K_{ri}-K_{rj})
\right)_{\alpha=1}^m.
\]
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Each block-sum-zero subspace is spanned by within-block basis differences. Applying CK gives the stated aggregated column differences.

records.title: Characterization of exact discrete lumping
records.label: thm:lumping_characterization
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Characterization of exact discrete lumping]\label{thm:lumping_characterization}
Let \(K\) be column stochastic. A coarse column stochastic matrix \(\overline K\) satisfying
\[
CK=\overline KC
\]
exists if and only if, for every source block \(B_\beta\), every pair \(i,j\in B_\beta\), and every target block \(B_\alpha\),
\[
\sum_{r\in B_\alpha}K_{ri}
=
\sum_{r\in B_\alpha}K_{rj}.
\]
When it exists, \(\overline K\) is unique and
\[
\overline K_{\alpha\beta}
=
\sum_{r\in B_\alpha}K_{ri}
\]
for any \(i\in B_\beta\).
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Column-by-column condition necessary and sufficient. Nonnegative aggregate entries and total column sum one preserve stochasticity.

records.title: Continuous time lumping
records.label: cor:continuous_lumping
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Continuous time lumping]\label{cor:continuous_lumping}
A coarse Markov generator \(\overline Q\) satisfying
\[
CQ=\overline QC
\]
exists if and only if the aggregated rates
\[
\sum_{r\in B_\alpha}Q_{ri}
\]
depend only on the source block of \(i\). In that case
\[
C\e^{tQ}=\e^{t\overline Q}C
\]
for every \(t\geq0\).
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Off-block aggregate rates are nonnegative; total coarse column sum zero. Bounded generator power series gives exact exponential intertwining.

records.title: Finite horizon lumping defect
records.label: thm:finite_horizon_lumping
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Finite horizon lumping defect]\label{thm:finite_horizon_lumping}
For arbitrary fine and coarse operators \(K\) and \(\overline K\), with the fixed aggregation map \(C\), set
\[
\Delta_K=CK-\overline KC.
\]
Then
\[
CK^n-\overline K^nC
=
\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}
\overline K^{n-1-j}\Delta_KK^j.
\]
If \(K\) and \(\overline K\) are column stochastic, then
\[
\norm{CK^n-\overline K^nC}_{1\to1}
\leq
n\norm{\Delta_K}_{1\to1}.
\]
For every probability vector \(p\), the total variation discrepancy is at most
\[
\frac n2\norm{\Delta_K}_{1\to1}.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Sum the telescoping identities
\[
\overline K^{n-1-j}CK^{j+1}
-
\overline K^{n-j}CK^j
=
\overline K^{n-1-j}\Delta_KK^j.
\]
Stochastic matrices are contractions in the \(\ell^1\) norm. The last statement uses total variation equal to one half of the \(\ell^1\) distance.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Correct telescoping order checked, including n=0 empty sum. Stochastic l1 operator norms are one; TV equals half l1.

records.title: Stationary mass descends
records.label: cor:stationary_descends
records.review_note: Apply CK=Kbar C to Kp=p. No converse or uniqueness of stationary laws asserted.

records.title: Finite conditional expectation
records.label: thm:finite_conditional_expectation
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Finite conditional expectation]\label{thm:finite_conditional_expectation}
The operator \(P_\mathcal Q\) is the orthogonal projector onto the functions that are constant on every block of \(\mathcal Q\). In particular,
\[
P_\mathcal Q^2=P_\mathcal Q,
\qquad
P_\mathcal Q^*=P_\mathcal Q.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Strictly positive pi prevents zero denominators. Weighted inner-product calculation establishes self-adjointness and blockwise idempotence.

records.title: Tower law and martingale packets
records.label: thm:martingale_packets
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Tower law and martingale packets]\label{thm:martingale_packets}
Let $P_0,P_1,\ldots,P_r$ come from increasingly fine partitions, so that
\[
\Ran P_0\subseteq\Ran P_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\Ran P_r.
\]
Define
\[
D_0=P_0,
\qquad
D_j=P_j-P_{j-1}
\quad(1\leq j\leq r).
\]
Then
\[
P_iP_j=P_{\min(i,j)},
\qquad
D_iD_j=\delta_{ij}D_j,
\qquad
P_r=\sum_{j=0}^rD_j.
\]
Every \(D_j\) is an orthogonal projector, and
\[
\norm{P_rf}_\pi^2
=
\sum_{j=0}^r\norm{D_jf}_\pi^2
\]
and
\[
\norm f_\pi^2
=
\sum_{j=0}^r\norm{D_jf}_\pi^2
+
\norm{f-P_rf}_\pi^2.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Nested orthogonal projections commute with product P_min. Differences are orthogonal idempotents, sum to P_r, and give Pythagorean energy.

records.title: Law of total variance
records.label: cor:total_variance
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Law of total variance]\label{cor:total_variance}
For a real valued \(f\), let \(P_0f=\Exp_\pi[f]\one\). Then
\[
\Var_\pi(f)
=
\Var_\pi(P_\mathcal Qf)
+
\norm{f-P_\mathcal Qf}_\pi^2.
\]
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Subtract global mean, then split into range P_Q and its orthogonal complement. Real-valued scope is explicit.

records.title: General conditional expectations
records.label: strengthened:standardfact:39
records.review_note: Imported background retained as such; exact external theorem not independently authenticated in this audit.

records.title: Ornstein Uhlenbeck semigroup
records.label: thm:ou_semigroup
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Ornstein Uhlenbeck semigroup]\label{thm:ou_semigroup}
The operators \((\Ocal_t)_{t\geq0}\) form a positive Markov contraction semigroup on \(L^p(\gamma)\) for every \(1\leq p\leq\infty\). On \(L^2(\gamma)\), the semigroup is self adjoint and
\[
\Ocal_t h_n=\e^{-nt}h_n.
\]
The family \((h_n)_{n\geq0}\) is an orthonormal basis of \(L^2(\gamma)\).
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Positivity and preservation of constants follow from the integral formula. If \(X\) and \(Y\) are independent standard Gaussian variables, then
\[
\e^{-s}
\left(
\e^{-t}x+\sqrt{1-\e^{-2t}}X
\right)
+
\sqrt{1-\e^{-2s}}Y
\]
has the same distribution as
\[
\e^{-(s+t)}x
+
\sqrt{1-\e^{-2(s+t)}}Z
\]
with \(Z\) standard Gaussian. This proves the semigroup law. Jensen's inequality and invariance of \(\gamma\) give the \(L^p\) contraction. The joint Gaussian pair
\[
\left(
X,
\e^{-t}X+\sqrt{1-\e^{-2t}}Y
\right)
\]
is symmetric under interchange, which proves self adjointness.

Apply \(\Ocal_t\) to the Hermite generating function. Gaussian integration gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Ocal_t
\exp\left(ux-\frac{u^2}{2}\right)
&=
\exp\left(
\e^{-t}ux-
\frac{\e^{-2t}u^2}{2}
\right)\\
&=
\sum_{n=0}^\infty
\e^{-nt}H_n(x)\frac{u^n}{n!}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Comparison of coefficients proves the eigenvalue formula. The same generating function shows
\[
\int H_mH_n\dd\gamma=n!\delta_{mn}.
\]
The Hermite polynomials span all polynomials, and polynomials are dense in \(L^2(\gamma)\). Hence the normalized family is an orthonormal basis. See \cite{Janson1997} for the general Gaussian Hilbert space setting.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Gaussian composition, Jensen and exchangeability give semigroup/contraction/self-adjointness; generating function gives eigenvalues and orthogonality. Polynomial density in Gaussian L2 is imported background, not established in this source. L-infinity strong continuity is not asserted.

records.title: Hermite packet reconstruction
records.label: cor:hermite_packets
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Hermite packet reconstruction]\label{cor:hermite_packets}
Let \(P_n\) be the orthogonal projection onto \(\CC h_n\). Then
\[
I=\sum_{n=0}^\infty P_n
\]
in the strong operator topology and
\[
\Ocal_t
=
\sum_{n=0}^\infty\e^{-nt}P_n.
\]
For \(f\in L^2(\gamma)\),
\[
\norm{\Ocal_t f}_2^2
=
\sum_{n=0}^\infty
\e^{-2nt}\norm{P_nf}_2^2.
\]
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Parseval and diagonal action yield strong reconstruction and energy, conditional on the Hermite-basis input. No operator-norm convergence of identity resolution is asserted.

records.title: Generator and Dirichlet form
records.label: prop:ou_generator
records.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Generator and Dirichlet form]\label{prop:ou_generator}
On the polynomial subspace, the infinitesimal generator of \((\Ocal_t)\) is the differential operator
\[
\Lcal f=f''-xf'.
\]
It satisfies
\[
\Lcal h_n=-nh_n.
\]
For every polynomial \(f\),
\[
\ip{-\Lcal f}{f}_{L^2(\gamma)}
=
\int_\RR\abs{f'(x)}^2\gamma(\dd x).
\]
\end{proposition}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Write
\[
\rho_t=\e^{-t}=1-t+O(t^2),
\qquad
\sigma_t^2=1-\e^{-2t}=2t+O(t^2).
\]
For a polynomial \(f\), Taylor expansion at \(x\) and Gaussian integration give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Ocal_tf(x)
={}&f(x)
+f'(x)(\rho_t-1)x
+\frac12f''(x)\sigma_t^2
+o(t)\\
={}&f(x)+t\bigl(f''(x)-xf'(x)\bigr)+o(t).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every omitted term is a polynomial in the Gaussian variable multiplied by a quantity that is \(o(t)\), so the expansion may be integrated term by term. Therefore
\[
\left.\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\Ocal_tf\right|_{t=0}
=f''-xf'.
\]
The Hermite eigenvalue identity also follows by differentiating
\(
\Ocal_th_n=\e^{-nt}h_n
\)
at zero. Gaussian integration by parts gives
\[
\int_\RR f'(x)\overline{g(x)}\gamma(\dd x)
=
\int_\RR f(x)\overline{xg(x)-g'(x)}\gamma(\dd x).
\]
Set \(g=f'\) and rearrange.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: For polynomials, finite Taylor expansion can be integrated coefficientwise; Gaussian odd moments vanish and higher surviving terms are o(t). Integration by parts gives stated Dirichlet form.

records.title: Gaussian spectral gap
records.label: cor:ou_spectral_gap
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Gaussian spectral gap]\label{cor:ou_spectral_gap}
If \(f\in L^2(\gamma)\) has mean zero, then
\[
\norm{\Ocal_tf}_2
\leq
\e^{-t}\norm f_2.
\]
For every polynomial \(f\),
\[
\Var_\gamma(f)
\leq
\int_\RR\abs{f'(x)}^2\gamma(\dd x).
\]
\end{corollary}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
A mean zero function has no \(h_0\) component, so every surviving Hermite multiplier is at most \(\e^{-t}\). For a polynomial
\[
f-\Exp_\gamma f=\sum_{n\geq1}c_nh_n.
\]
Then
\[
\Var_\gamma(f)=\sum_{n\geq1}\abs{c_n}^2
\leq
\sum_{n\geq1}n\abs{c_n}^2
=
\ip{-\Lcal f}{f}.
\]
Apply \cref{prop:ou_generator}.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Mean-zero coefficients begin at n=1; exp(-nt)≤exp(-t). Polynomial energy sum weights n≥1. Depends on complete Hermite basis.

records.title: Fractional Hermite transfer
records.label: cor:fractional_hermite
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Fractional Hermite transfer]\label{cor:fractional_hermite}
Let \(-\Lcal\) be the nonnegative Ornstein Uhlenbeck number operator with
\[
-\Lcal h_n=nh_n.
\]
For every \(\alpha>0\),
\[
\e^{-t(-\Lcal)^\alpha}f
=
\sum_{n=0}^\infty
\e^{-tn^\alpha}P_nf.
\]
This is a contraction semigroup on \(L^2(\gamma)\).
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Diagonal nonnegative self-adjoint number operator defines fractional semigroup for any alpha>0. Claim is an L2 contraction, not positivity for alpha>1.

records.title: Scale invariance and composition
records.label: prop:bayes_composition
records.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Scale invariance and composition]\label{prop:bayes_composition}
For every \(c>0\),
\[
\Bcal_{c\lambda}=\Bcal_\lambda.
\]
If all relevant evidences are positive, then
\[
\Bcal_\mu(\Bcal_\lambda(p))
=
\Bcal_{\lambda\odot\mu}(p).
\]
\end{proposition}
records.review_note: Positive evidences ensure denominators nonzero; likelihood scaling and sequential normalizers cancel.

records.title: Bayesian packet reconstruction
records.label: thm:bayesian_packet_reconstruction
records.review_note: Each nonzero packet evidence contributes exactly lambda_i p_i/Z. Zero-evidence packets have zero posterior mass and need no conditional shape.

records.title: Likelihood perturbation
records.label: thm:likelihood_perturbation
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Likelihood perturbation]\label{thm:likelihood_perturbation}
Let \(\lambda,\mu\geq0\) have positive evidences under a fixed prior \(p\). Set
\[
d_p(\lambda,\mu)
=
\sum_i\abs{\lambda_i-\mu_i}p_i.
\]
Then
\[
\norm{\Bcal_\lambda(p)-\Bcal_\mu(p)}_1
\leq
\frac{2d_p(\lambda,\mu)}
{\max\{Z_\lambda(p),Z_\mu(p)\}}.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Add and subtract \(\mu\odot p/Z_\lambda(p)\). This gives
\[
\norm{\Bcal_\lambda(p)-\Bcal_\mu(p)}_1
\leq
\frac{2d_p(\lambda,\mu)}{Z_\lambda(p)}.
\]
Interchanging \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\) gives the same estimate with \(Z_\mu(p)\). Take the smaller of the two upper bounds.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Both numerator perturbation and evidence perturbation are bounded by weighted absolute difference. Swap likelihoods and take smaller bound, producing max evidence in denominator.

records.title: Stability with respect to the prior
records.label: thm:prior_stability
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Stability with respect to the prior]\label{thm:prior_stability}
Assume
\[
0<a\leq\lambda_i\leq b
\]
for every \(i\). Then
\[
\norm{\Bcal_\lambda(p)-\Bcal_\lambda(q)}_1
\leq
\frac{2b}{a}\norm{p-q}_1
\]
for all priors \(p,q\in\Delta_{n-1}\).
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Evidence≥a>0 and numerator/evidence perturbations each ≤b||p-q||1; factor2b/a is valid though not claimed sharp.

records.title: Exact two stage Bayesian update
records.label: thm:two_stage_bayes
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Exact two stage Bayesian update]\label{thm:two_stage_bayes}
For every strictly positive prior,
\[
C\Bcal_\lambda(p)
=
\Bcal_{\overline\lambda(p)}(Cp).
\]
For every packet with \(\overline\lambda_\alpha(p)>0\), the posterior conditional distribution is
\[
q_{\alpha,i}
=
\frac{\lambda_ir_{\alpha,i}}
{\overline\lambda_\alpha(p)}.
\]
A packet with zero average likelihood has zero posterior mass. Thus a fine Bayesian update consists of a coarse update by packet average likelihoods followed by independent local updates inside the packets that survive.
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Split p into block mass and positive conditional prior; packet evidences factor and local formula follows. Zero-evidence packets are explicitly excluded from conditionals.

records.title: Characterization of fixed coarse sufficiency
records.label: thm:bayesian_sufficiency
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Characterization of fixed coarse sufficiency]\label{thm:bayesian_sufficiency}
Assume \(\lambda_i>0\) for every state. The following conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a positive coarse likelihood \(\ell\in(0,\infty)^m\) such that
\[
C\Bcal_\lambda(p)
=
\Bcal_\ell(Cp)
\]
for every strictly positive prior \(p\), and the posterior conditional distribution inside every packet equals its prior conditional distribution.
\item The likelihood is constant on every packet.
\end{enumerate}
When these conditions hold, \(\ell_\alpha\) can be chosen as the common value of \(\lambda\) on \(I_\alpha\), and it is unique up to a common positive scale.
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Definition includes preservation of every within-packet conditional, so single-block case also forces constant likelihood. Positivity allows cancellation; coarse likelihood unique only up to common scale. This differs from mass-only sufficiency in the formal core.

records.title: Coarsest fixed sufficient partition
records.label: thm:coarsest_bayesian_partition
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Coarsest fixed sufficient partition]\label{thm:coarsest_bayesian_partition}
Let \(\mathcal L\) be a nonempty family of strictly positive likelihood vectors. Define
\[
i\sim_{\mathcal L}j
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\lambda_i=\lambda_j
\quad\hbox{for every }\lambda\in\mathcal L.
\]
Let \(\mathcal Q_{\mathcal L}\) be the partition into equivalence classes. A partition \(\mathcal Q\) gives a fixed coarse sufficient description in the sense of \cref{thm:bayesian_sufficiency} for every \(\lambda\in\mathcal L\) if and only if every block of \(\mathcal Q\) is contained in a block of \(\mathcal Q_{\mathcal L}\). Hence \(\mathcal Q_{\mathcal L}\) is the unique coarsest partition with this property.
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Block constancy for every likelihood is equivalent to refining common level sets. Holds even for a single common class under the stronger conditional-preservation definition.

records.title: Within packet information loss
records.label: strengthened:definition:52
records.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Within packet information loss]
For a prior \(p\), define
\[
\eta_i(p)
=
\lambda_i-\overline\lambda_\alpha(p)
\quad\hbox{when }i\in I_\alpha.
\]
Then
\[
\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}r_{\alpha,i}\eta_i(p)=0.
\]
\end{definition}
records.review_note: Context, definition, example, or scope remark read; not counted as a proved result.

records.title: Exact local distortion
records.label: prop:local_bayes_distortion
records.review_note: Subtract local normalized prior; absolute deviations average to exact l1 error. Average likelihood bounded below by packet minimum.

records.title: Approximate coarse Bayesian rule
records.label: thm:approximate_coarse_bayes
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Block constancy gives
\[
C\Bcal_{\widetilde\lambda}(p)
=
\Bcal_\ell(Cp).
\]
Aggregation is an \(\ell^1\) contraction. Apply \cref{thm:likelihood_perturbation} to the two fine posteriors and then aggregate.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Aggregation is l1-contractive; block-constant surrogate likelihood commutes with aggregation. Positive evidence for original update remains required by section setup.

records.title: Relative information
records.label: strengthened:definition:55
records.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Relative information]
For probability vectors \(q\) and \(p\), define
\[
D(q\Vert p)
=
\sum_iq_i\log\frac{q_i}{p_i}.
\]
The convention is \(0\log0=0\). A term with \(q_i>0\) and \(p_i=0\) has value \(+\infty\).
\end{definition}
records.review_note: Context, definition, example, or scope remark read; not counted as a proved result.

records.title: Exact information decomposition
records.label: thm:bayesian_information_chain
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Exact information decomposition]\label{thm:bayesian_information_chain}
Let \(p\) and \(q\) be probability vectors on a finite partition \((I_\alpha)_\alpha\), and assume \(q_i=0\) whenever \(p_i=0\). Let
\[
m=Cp,
\qquad
n=Cq,
\]
and let \(p_\alpha\) and \(q_\alpha\) be the conditional distributions inside packet \(I_\alpha\) whenever the corresponding mass is positive. Then
\[
D(q\Vert p)
=
D(n\Vert m)
+
\sum_{\alpha:n_\alpha>0}
 n_\alpha D(q_\alpha\Vert p_\alpha).
\]
The first term is the information retained by the coarse masses. The second term is the exact information carried by changes inside the packets.
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
For \(i\in I_\alpha\), write
\[
p_i=m_\alpha p_{\alpha,i},
\qquad
q_i=n_\alpha q_{\alpha,i}.
\]
Then
\[
\log\frac{q_i}{p_i}
=
\log\frac{n_\alpha}{m_\alpha}
+
\log\frac{q_{\alpha,i}}{p_{\alpha,i}}.
\]
Multiply by \(q_i\), sum first inside each packet, and then sum over the packets. This is the finite relative entropy chain rule. Standard information theoretic treatments include \cite{CoverThomas2006}.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Finite relative-entropy chain rule by p_i=m_alpha p_alpha,i and q_i=n_alpha q_alpha,i. Restrict logarithmic algebra to q_i>0; null terms follow by convention. q<

records.title: Coarse data processing and equality
records.label: cor:coarse_data_processing
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Coarse data processing and equality]\label{cor:coarse_data_processing}
Under the assumptions of \cref{thm:bayesian_information_chain},
\[
D(Cq\Vert Cp)
\leq
D(q\Vert p).
\]
Equality holds if and only if
\[
q_\alpha=p_\alpha
\]
for every packet with positive posterior mass.
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Conditional KL≥0, with equality exactly equal conditional distributions, yields statement. Gibbs inequality is ordinary background; no parametric statistical sufficiency inferred.

records.title: Information created by a Bayesian update
records.label: cor:bayesian_information_gain
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Information created by a Bayesian update]\label{cor:bayesian_information_gain}
Let \(q=\Bcal_\lambda(p)\) with positive likelihood and positive prior. Then
\[
D(q\Vert p)
=
\sum_iq_i\log\lambda_i
-
\log Z_\lambda(p).
\]
Inside a packet,
\[
D(q_\alpha\Vert r_\alpha)
=
\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}
q_{\alpha,i}
\log\frac{\lambda_i}{\overline\lambda_\alpha(p)}.
\]
Hence
\[
D(q_\alpha\Vert r_\alpha)
\leq
\log
\frac{\max_{i\in I_\alpha}\lambda_i}
{\min_{i\in I_\alpha}\lambda_i}.
\]
\end{corollary}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
The posterior ratio is
\[
\frac{q_i}{p_i}
=
\frac{\lambda_i}{Z_\lambda(p)}.
\]
The local ratio is
\[
\frac{q_{\alpha,i}}{r_{\alpha,i}}
=
\frac{\lambda_i}{\overline\lambda_\alpha(p)}.
\]
Insert these identities into the definition of relative entropy. The final estimate follows because both \(\lambda_i\) and the packet average lie between the packet minimum and maximum.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Insert posterior/prior ratios. Both lambda and its packet average lie between positive min and max, yielding logarithmic bound.

records.title: Information criterion for local sufficiency
records.label: cor:information_sufficiency
records.review_note: All positive packets have positive posterior mass, so vanishing conditional KL gives equal local distributions and forces likelihood constancy.

records.label: strengthened:remark:60
records.review_note: Context, definition, example, or scope remark read; not counted as a proved result.

records.title: Bayesian flow and replicator equation
records.label: thm:bayesian_flow
records.section: Bayesian flows and hidden Markov recursion
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Bayesian flow and replicator equation]\label{thm:bayesian_flow}
The maps \(\Phi_t\) form a nonlinear semigroup:
\[
\Phi_{s+t}=\Phi_s\circ\Phi_t.
\]
Every coordinate satisfies
\[
\frac{\dd}{\dd t}p_i(t)
=
\bigl(g_i-\ip{g}{p(t)}\bigr)p_i(t).
\]
The support of \(p(t)\) is independent of \(t\), and for any two coordinates in the support,
\[
\frac{p_i(t)}{p_j(t)}
=
\e^{t(g_i-g_j)}
\frac{p_i(0)}{p_j(0)}.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Multiplying exponential likelihoods gives nonlinear semigroup. Quotient derivative, support preservation, and exact posterior odds agree.

records.title: Evidence cumulants and score monotonicity
records.label: thm:evidence_cumulants
records.section: Bayesian flows and hidden Markov recursion
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Evidence cumulants and score monotonicity]\label{thm:evidence_cumulants}
Set
\[
\psi(t)
=
\log\left(
\sum_i\e^{tg_i}p_i(0)
\right).
\]
Then
\[
\psi'(t)=\ip{g}{p(t)},
\qquad
\psi''(t)=\Var_{p(t)}(g)\geq0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\ip{g}{p(t)}
=
\Var_{p(t)}(g).
\]
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Twice differentiate finite log sum to get mean then centered second moment; derivative of score mean is variance.

records.title: Concentration on the maximal score packet
records.label: cor:bayes_flow_concentration
records.section: Bayesian flows and hidden Markov recursion
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Concentration on the maximal score packet]\label{cor:bayes_flow_concentration}
Let
\[
G=\max\{g_i:p_i(0)>0\}
\]
and let \(M\) be the set of supported indices with score \(G\). If \(M\) is the full support, then the conclusion below is immediate. Otherwise, suppose
\[
\delta
=
\min\{G-g_i:p_i(0)>0,
\quad i\notin M\}>0.
\]
Then
\[
1-\sum_{i\in M}p_i(t)
\leq
\frac{1-p_M(0)}{p_M(0)}\e^{-\delta t},
\]
where \(p_M(0)=\sum_{i\in M}p_i(0)\).
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Factor maximum supported score. The supported maximum packet has positive initial mass; outside weight is ≤(1-p_M)exp(-delta t). Full-support-max case is separately acknowledged.

records.title: Simplex preservation
records.label: prop:hmm_preservation
records.section: Bayesian flows and hidden Markov recursion
records.review_note: Column stochastic prediction followed by positive-evidence normalization preserves simplex.

records.title: One step filter stability
records.label: thm:hmm_stability
records.section: Bayesian flows and hidden Markov recursion
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Apply \cref{thm:prior_stability} to \(Kp\) and \(\widetilde Kq\). Then use
\[
\norm{Kp-\widetilde Kq}_1
\leq
\norm{K(p-q)}_1
+
\norm{(K-\widetilde K)q}_1
\]
and the stochastic contraction property.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Insert stochastic contraction estimate ||Kp-Ktilde q||1≤||p-q||1+||K-Ktilde||1 and apply prior-stability constant.

records.title: Beta binomial transfer
records.label: strengthened:example:66
records.section: Bayesian flows and hidden Markov recursion
records.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[Beta binomial transfer]
A beta prior with parameters \((a,b)\) and binomial data containing \(s\) successes in \(n\) trials gives the posterior parameters
\[
(a+s,b+n-s).
\]
The update is additive in the two exponent coordinates. This is a finite dimensional conjugate realization of likelihood composition. Standard Bayesian references include \cite{BernardoSmith1994}.
\end{example}
records.review_note: Context, definition, example, or scope remark read; not counted as a proved result.

records.title: Fractional packet calculus
records.label: thm:fractional_packet_calculus
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Fractional packet calculus]\label{thm:fractional_packet_calculus}
For \(\alpha,\beta>0\),
\[
L^\alpha L^\beta=L^{\alpha+\beta}.
\]
For \(s,t\geq0\),
\[
T_\alpha(s)T_\alpha(t)=T_\alpha(s+t).
\]
Every spectral packet \(P_jH\) reduces \(L^\alpha\) and \(T_\alpha(t)\).
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: All operations diagonal on a finite positive self-adjoint spectral decomposition; zero eigenvalues allowed for positive alpha,beta.

records.title: Balakrishnan formula in finite dimension
records.label: thm:balakrishnan
records.review_note: Reduce to scalar beta integral with 0<alpha<1. Zero eigenvalue contributes zero, and finite sum permits norm integral. Scalar Euler beta/reflection identity is imported elementary analytic background.

records.title: Exact fractional naturality
records.label: thm:exact_fractional_naturality
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Exact fractional naturality]\label{thm:exact_fractional_naturality}
Let \(L_f\) and \(L_c\) be finite dimensional positive self adjoint operators and let \(C\) satisfy
\[
CL_f=L_cC.
\]
Then, for every \(\alpha>0\) and \(t\geq0\),
\[
CL_f^\alpha=L_c^\alpha C
\]
and
\[
C\e^{-tL_f^\alpha}
=
\e^{-tL_c^\alpha}C.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: One polynomial interpolates each scalar function on the finite union of spectra, so rectangular intertwining passes to it without a gap assumption.

records.title: Fractional defect bound
records.label: thm:fractional_defect
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Fractional defect bound]\label{thm:fractional_defect}
Let \(0<\alpha<1\). Suppose
\[
L_f\geq mI,
\qquad
L_c\geq mI
\]
for some \(m>0\). Define
\[
\Delta_L=CL_f-L_cC.
\]
Then
\[
\norm{CL_f^\alpha-L_c^\alpha C}
\leq
\alpha m^{\alpha-1}\norm{\Delta_L}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\norm{
C\e^{-tL_f^\alpha}
-
\e^{-tL_c^\alpha}C
}
\leq
\alpha t m^{\alpha-1}\norm{\Delta_L}.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Set
\[
R_f(s)=(sI+L_f)^{-1},
\qquad
R_c(s)=(sI+L_c)^{-1}.
\]
The resolvent identity gives
\[
CR_f(s)-R_c(s)C
=
-R_c(s)\Delta_LR_f(s).
\]
Since \(LR=I-sR\),
\[
CL_fR_f(s)-L_cR_c(s)C
=
sR_c(s)\Delta_LR_f(s).
\]
Insert this into \cref{thm:balakrishnan}. The spectral lower bound gives
\[
\norm{R_f(s)},\norm{R_c(s)}
\leq
\frac{1}{s+m}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\norm{CL_f^\alpha-L_c^\alpha C}
&\leq
\frac{\sin(\pi\alpha)}{\pi}
\norm{\Delta_L}
\int_0^\infty
\frac{s^\alpha}{(s+m)^2}\dd s\\
&=
\alpha m^{\alpha-1}\norm{\Delta_L}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The semigroup estimate follows from \cref{thm:duhamel_defect}, applied to the contraction generators \(-L_f^\alpha\) and \(-L_c^\alpha\).
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Sign checked: C R_f-R_c C=−R_c Delta_L R_f; L R=I−sR gives positive sR_c Delta_L R_f. Resolvent bound (s+m)^−1 and beta integral yield alpha m^(alpha−1). Duhamel generators are −L^alpha.

records.title: Stable subordination
records.label: fact:stable_subordination
records.statement_tex:
\begin{standardfact}[Stable subordination]\label{fact:stable_subordination}
Let \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(t>0\). There is a probability measure \(\eta_{\alpha,t}\) on \([0,\infty)\) such that
\[
\int_0^\infty \e^{-s\lambda}\eta_{\alpha,t}(\dd s)
=
\e^{-t\lambda^\alpha}
\]
for every \(\lambda\geq0\). Consequently, for a finite dimensional positive self adjoint operator,
\[
\e^{-tL^\alpha}
=
\int_0^\infty
\e^{-sL}\eta_{\alpha,t}(\dd s)
\]
in operator norm. The measures satisfy the convolution law
\[
\eta_{\alpha,s}*\eta_{\alpha,t}
=
\eta_{\alpha,s+t}.
\]
\end{standardfact}

records.title: Exact nodal Green reconstruction
records.label: thm:nodal_green
records.section: Green operators and finite difference transfer
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
The inverse of the unscaled tridiagonal matrix has entry
\[
\frac{\min(i,j)(n+1-\max(i,j))}{n+1}.
\]
Multiplying by \(h^2\) and dividing by \(h\) gives
\[
h\min(i,j)
\left(1-\frac{\max(i,j)}{n+1}\right)
=
\min(x_i,x_j)-x_ix_j.
\]
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Discrete inverse entries equal min(i,j)(n+1-max(i,j))/(n+1). Scaling h² then dividing by h yields min(x_i,x_j)−x_i x_j. n≥1 implicit interior-node setting.

records.title: Discrete Green quadrature
records.label: cor:discrete_green_quadrature
records.section: Green operators and finite difference transfer
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Discrete Green quadrature]\label{cor:discrete_green_quadrature}
If \(u^h\) solves
\[
L_hu^h=f^h,
\]
then every nodal value has the exact representation
\[
u_i^h
=
h\sum_{j=1}^nG(x_i,x_j)f_j^h.
\]
Thus the discrete Green operator is the nodal rectangle quadrature of the continuum Green kernel.
\end{corollary}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
By \cref{thm:nodal_green},
\[
(L_h^{-1})_{ij}=hG(x_i,x_j).
\]
Multiply the inverse matrix by the source vector.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Multiply exact inverse entries hG(x_i,x_j) by arbitrary nodal source. This is an exact discrete representation, not a continuum error assertion.

records.title: Discrete maximum bound
records.label: prop:discrete_inverse_bound
records.section: Green operators and finite difference transfer
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Nonnegativity follows from the entry formula in \cref{thm:nodal_green}. Let \(v_i=x_i(1-x_i)/2\). Since the second difference is exact on quadratics,
\[
L_hv=\one.
\]
Hence the \(i\)th row sum of \(L_h^{-1}\) is \(v_i\). For a nonnegative matrix, the infinity operator norm is the largest row sum.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Nonnegative inverse makes infinity norm max row sum. Quadratic barrier v_i=x_i(1-x_i)/2 solves L_h v=1 and max≤1/8.

records.title: Second order Poisson solution error
records.label: thm:poisson_error
records.section: Green operators and finite difference transfer
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Second order Poisson solution error]\label{thm:poisson_error}
Suppose \(u\in C^4[0,1]\) solves the Dirichlet problem above. Let
\[
f^h_i=f(x_i)
\]
and let \(u^h\) solve
\[
L_hu^h=f^h.
\]
Then
\[
\max_i\abs{u^h_i-u(x_i)}
\leq
\frac{h^2}{96}
\norm{u^{(4)}}_\infty.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Taylor expansion with remainder gives
\[
\norm{L_h(u(x_i))_i-f^h}_\infty
\leq
\frac{h^2}{12}\norm{u^{(4)}}_\infty.
\]
Apply \(L_h^{-1}\) and use \cref{prop:discrete_inverse_bound}.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: C4 consistency error≤h²||D4u||∞/12 multiplied by inverse norm≤1/8 gives h²/96. Dirichlet endpoints used.

records.title: Low mode eigenvalue control
records.label: thm:low_mode
records.section: Green operators and finite difference transfer
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Low mode eigenvalue control]\label{thm:low_mode}
For \(kh\leq1\),
\[
0\leq(k\pi)^2-\lambda_{k,h}
\leq
\frac{(k\pi)^4}{12}h^2.
\]
Consequently, for every fixed \(k\),
\[
\lambda_{k,h}=(k\pi)^2+O(h^2).
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Set \(x=k\pi h/2\). The condition \(kh\leq1\) gives \(0\leq x\leq\pi/2\). On this interval,
\[
\sin x\geq x-\frac{x^3}{6},
\]
so
\[
0\leq x^2-\sin^2x\leq\frac{x^4}{3}.
\]
Multiply by \(4/h^2\).
\end{proof}
records.review_note: With x=k*pi*h/2 in [0,pi/2], x−x³/6≥0 and sin x≥that expression. Squaring yields x²−sin²x≤x⁴/3. Physical modes have 1≤k≤n.

records.title: Heat and fractional mode transfer
records.label: cor:mode_transfer
records.section: Green operators and finite difference transfer
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Heat and fractional mode transfer]\label{cor:mode_transfer}
Let \(\lambda_k=(k\pi)^2\). For \(t\geq0\),
\[
0\leq
\e^{-t\lambda_{k,h}}-\e^{-t\lambda_k}
\leq
\frac{t(k\pi)^4}{12}h^2\e^{-t\lambda_{k,h}}.
\]
For \(0<\alpha\leq1\) and fixed \(k\),
\[
\lambda_{k,h}^\alpha
=
\lambda_k^\alpha+O(h^2)
\]
and
\[
\e^{-t\lambda_{k,h}^\alpha}
=
\e^{-t\lambda_k^\alpha}+O(th^2)
\]
uniformly for \(t\) in bounded intervals.
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Mean-value estimate for heat exponentials gives t(delta lambda)exp(-t lambda_h). Fixed k ensures positive common interval for fractional derivatives; no uniform-in-all-modes claim.

records.title: Discrete Feynman Kac formula
records.label: thm:discrete_feynman_kac
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Discrete Feynman Kac formula]\label{thm:discrete_feynman_kac}
Define
\[
M_V=\diag(\e^{-V})K^T.
\]
For terminal data \(f\),
\[
(M_V^nf)_i
=
\Exp_i\left[
\exp\left(
-\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}V(X_r)
\right)
f(X_n)
\right].
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
For one step,
\[
(M_Vf)_i
=
\e^{-V(i)}\sum_jK_{ji}f_j.
\]
Iterating expands the matrix product over all paths. The product of transition entries is the path probability, and the diagonal factors give the exponential potential weight.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: K is column stochastic, so functions use K^T. Potential is applied at X_0,...,X_(n−1), terminal f at X_n; multiplication order matches.

records.title: Continuous time finite state formula
records.label: thm:continuous_feynman_kac
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Continuous time finite state formula]\label{thm:continuous_feynman_kac}
Let \(Q\) be a finite Markov generator and let \((X_t)_{t\geq0}\) be the corresponding chain. Then
\[
\left(
\e^{t(Q^T-D_V)}f
\right)_i
=
\Exp_i\left[
\exp\left(
-\int_0^tV(X_s)\dd s
\right)
f(X_t)
\right].
\]
If \(V\geq v_0\), then
\[
\norm{\e^{t(Q^T-D_V)}}_{\infty\to\infty}
\leq
\e^{-v_0t}.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Conditioning over the first small time interval gives the backward equation
\[
\dot u=(Q^T-D_V)u,
\qquad
u(0)=f.
\]
The finite system has a unique solution, namely the displayed matrix exponential. The expectation bound follows from
\[
\exp\left(-\int_0^tV(X_s)\dd s\right)
\leq
\e^{-v_0t}.
\]
This finite argument is the matrix form of the Feynman Kac principle originating in \cite{Kac1949}.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Finite-state conditioning produces generator Q^T−D_V and unique matrix ODE solution. Real V bounded automatically in finite state, with supnorm bound for V≥v0.

records.title: Alternating propagation and killing
records.label: thm:feynman_kac_product
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Set \(B=-D_V\) and \(C=Q^T\). For bounded matrices,
\[
\e^{tB/n}\e^{tC/n}
=
I+\frac{t}{n}(B+C)+O(n^{-2})
\]
uniformly in operator norm. The standard telescoping comparison with
\(
(I+t(B+C)/n)^n
\)
shows that the product converges to \(\e^{t(B+C)}\). This is the displayed factor order, so the limit follows.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Each one-step product differs from I+t(B+C)/n by O(n^−2); bounded product norms give O(n^−1) telescoping error. Order exp(B)exp(C) matches backward weighting.

records.title: Schur Feshbach resolvent
records.label: thm:feshbach_resolvent
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Schur Feshbach resolvent]\label{thm:feshbach_resolvent}
Assume \(zI-A_{QQ}\) is invertible. Then \(zI-A\) is invertible if and only if \(F_P(z)\) is invertible. In that case,
\[
P(zI-A)^{-1}P
=
F_P(z)^{-1}.
\]
In finite dimension,
\[
\det(zI-A)
=
\det(zI-A_{QQ})\det F_P(z).
\]
\end{theorem}
records.review_note: Block product L_z S_z gives correct off-diagonal minus signs and retained block zI−A_PP. Triangular inversion establishes compressed resolvent. P-resolvent-P is identified with restriction to X_P.

records.title: Memory and self energy
records.label: thm:memory_self_energy
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Memory and self energy]\label{thm:memory_self_energy}
If \(z\) lies to the right of the spectrum of \(A_{QQ}\), then
\[
\int_0^\infty
\e^{-zt}\Kcal(t)\dd t
=
\Sigma_P(z).
\]
If
\[
\norm{\e^{tA_{QQ}}}
\leq
M\e^{-\gamma t},
\]
then
\[
\norm{\Kcal(t)}
\leq
M\norm{A_{PQ}}\norm{A_{QP}}\e^{-\gamma t}
\]
and
\[
\norm{\Kcal}_{L^1(0,\infty)}
\leq
\frac{M}{\gamma}
\norm{A_{PQ}}\norm{A_{QP}}.
\]
\end{theorem}

records.review_note: Raw decay claim lacks gamma>0. Spectral half-plane Laplace identity for bounded Banach hidden operator requires spectral/growth argument, now supplied to editor and checked against Engel-Nagel IV.3.12(iv).

records.title: Criterion for exact local closure
records.label: thm:local_closure
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Criterion for exact local closure]\label{thm:local_closure}
Assume \(x_Q(0)=0\). The following conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every retained initial state,
\[
P\e^{tA}P
=
\e^{tA_{PP}}P
\]
for all \(t\geq0\).
\item \(\Sigma_P(z)=0\) for every sufficiently large \(z\).
\item \(\Kcal(t)=0\) for every \(t\geq0\).
\item If \(d=\dim X_Q\), then
\[
A_{PQ}A_{QQ}^kA_{QP}=0
\]
for \(0\leq k<d\).
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
By \cref{thm:laplace_packet_resolvent}, the Laplace transform of the projected propagator is the projected resolvent. By \cref{thm:feshbach_resolvent}, the first condition is equivalent to
\[
(zI-A_{PP}-\Sigma_P(z))^{-1}
=
(zI-A_{PP})^{-1}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(z\), which is equivalent to the second condition. The second and third conditions are equivalent by \cref{thm:memory_self_energy} and uniqueness of the Laplace transform.

For large \(z\),
\[
\Sigma_P(z)
=
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}
\frac{A_{PQ}A_{QQ}^kA_{QP}}{z^{k+1}}.
\]
Thus the second condition implies the moment identities. Conversely, the first \(d\) identities imply all later ones by the Cayley Hamilton theorem, so the series vanishes.
\end{proof}

records.review_note: Resolvent equality, Laplace uniqueness and memory-zero equivalent in bounded setting; finite first-d-moment criterion uses Cayley-Hamilton and requires dim X_Q=d<infinity explicit.

records.title: Polynomial exponential memory of a finite hidden system
records.label: thm:modal_memory
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
The primary decomposition gives
\[
A_{QQ}Q_j=\mu_jQ_j+N_j
\]
with commuting scalar and nilpotent parts on \(Q_jX_Q\). Therefore
\[
\e^{tA_{QQ}}Q_j
=
\e^{\mu_jt}
\sum_{k=0}^{\nu_j-1}
\frac{t^k}{k!}N_j^kQ_j.
\]
Multiplication by \(A_{PQ}\) and \(A_{QP}\) gives the memory formula. On the \(j\)th primary space, the nilpotent resolvent expansion is
\[
(zI-A_{QQ})^{-1}Q_j
=
\sum_{k=0}^{\nu_j-1}
\frac{N_j^kQ_j}{(z-\mu_j)^{k+1}}.
\]
Multiplication by the coupling blocks gives the self energy formula for every \(z\) outside the hidden spectrum. Equivalently, on a right half plane it is the Laplace transform identity
\[
\int_0^\infty
\e^{-zt}\e^{\mu_jt}
\frac{t^k}{k!}
\dd t
=
\frac{1}{(z-\mu_j)^{k+1}}.
\]
Under stability,
\[
\int_0^\infty
\e^{\operatorname{Re}\mu_jt}
\frac{t^k}{k!}
\dd t
=
\frac{1}{(-\operatorname{Re}\mu_j)^{k+1}}.
\]
Sum the omitted terms.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Primary projections commute with A; nilpotent exponential and resolvent expansions have coefficients B_j,k/k! and pole order k+1. Integral of exp(Re mu t)t^k/k! is (−Re mu)^−k−1. Whole primary blocks retained; nonnormal projections need not be orthogonal.

records.title: Optimal selection for the certified primary block bound
records.label: cor:optimal_primary_selection
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Optimal selection for the certified primary block bound]\label{cor:optimal_primary_selection}
Under the stable assumptions of \cref{thm:modal_memory}, define the primary block weights
\[
w_j
=
\sum_{k=0}^{\nu_j-1}
\frac{\norm{B_{j,k}}}
{(-\operatorname{Re}\mu_j)^{k+1}}.
\]
Among all sets \(J\) containing \(k\) primary blocks, the certified upper bound
\[
\sum_{j\notin J}w_j
\]
is minimized by retaining the \(k\) largest weights. If
\[
w_{(1)}\geq w_{(2)}\geq\cdots\geq w_{(r)},
\]
then the least number of retained primary blocks certified to give \(L^1\) error at most \(\varepsilon\) is the least \(k\) for which
\[
\sum_{j>k}w_{(j)}\leq\varepsilon.
\]
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Exchange argument minimizes omitted nonnegative weight sum for a fixed number of whole primary blocks. It does not optimize actual L1 error, retained dimension, or real conjugate-pair constraints.

records.title: Normal hidden dynamics
records.label: cor:normal_modal_memory
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Normal hidden dynamics]\label{cor:normal_modal_memory}
Suppose \(X_Q\) is a finite dimensional Hilbert space. If \(A_{QQ}\) is normal with spectral resolution
\[
A_{QQ}=\sum_{j=1}^r\mu_jQ_j,
\]
then
\[
\Kcal(t)=\sum_{j=1}^r\e^{\mu_jt}B_j,
\qquad
\Sigma_P(z)=\sum_{j=1}^r\frac{B_j}{z-\mu_j},
\]
where
\[
B_j=A_{PQ}Q_jA_{QP}.
\]
If \(\operatorname{Re}\mu_j<0\), then
\[
\norm{\Kcal-\Kcal_J}_{L^1(0,\infty)}
\leq
\sum_{j\notin J}
\frac{\norm{B_j}}{-\operatorname{Re}\mu_j}.
\]
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Normal finite operator has zero nilpotent parts and orthogonal spectral projections; specialize general modal result.

records.title: Pole order and hidden Jordan depth

records.review_note: Principal parts at distinct poles cannot cancel across eigenvalues. Highest nonzero coefficient determines pole order; zero highest coefficient permits lower order.

records.title: Finite auxiliary state realization
records.label: cor:finite_auxiliary_realization
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Finite auxiliary state realization]\label{cor:finite_auxiliary_realization}
Every kernel of the form
\[
\Kcal(t)=B\e^{tD}C
\]
can be represented exactly by adjoining the finite auxiliary state
\[
\dot y=Dy+Cx_P,
\qquad
\dot x_P=A_{PP}x_P+By,
\qquad
y(0)=0.
\]
A nonzero auxiliary initial state adds the explicit forcing \(B\e^{tD}y(0)\). The self energy of the augmented system is
\[
B(zI-D)^{-1}C.
\]
\end{corollary}
records.review_note: Variation of constants for y with y(0)=0 gives convolution. Nonzero initial hidden state gives explicit forcing; no stability asserted.

records.title: Volterra stability under kernel compression
records.label: thm:volterra_compression
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Volterra stability under kernel compression]\label{thm:volterra_compression}
Let \(S(t)\) be a semigroup on a Banach space with
\[
\norm{S(t)}\leq M_T
\quad(0\leq t\leq T).
\]
Let \(K,\widetilde K\in L^1((0,T),\mathcal B(X))\). Suppose \(x\) and \(\widetilde x\) solve the same mild equation with the same initial state and forcing, except that \(K\) is replaced by \(\widetilde K\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
x(t)
={}&S(t)x_0+
\int_0^tS(t-s)g(s)\dd s\\
&+
\int_0^tS(t-s)
\int_0^sK(s-r)x(r)\dd r\dd s.
\end{aligned}
\]
Assume
\[
\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\norm{\widetilde x(t)}\leq B.
\]
Set
\[
L=\norm K_{L^1(0,T)},
\qquad
\varepsilon=\norm{K-\widetilde K}_{L^1(0,T)}.
\]
Then
\[
\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}
\norm{x(t)-\widetilde x(t)}
\leq
M_TBT\varepsilon
\exp(M_TLT).
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Let
\[
E(t)=\sup_{0\leq r\leq t}\norm{x(r)-\widetilde x(r)}.
\]
Subtract the two mild equations. Fubini's theorem and the triangle inequality give
\[
E(t)
\leq
M_TL\int_0^tE(r)\dd r
+
M_TBt\varepsilon.
\]
For \(t\leq T\), replace the last factor \(t\) by \(T\) and apply Gronwall's inequality.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Subtract mild equations, use K*(x−xtilde)+(K−Ktilde)*xtilde. Fubini yields M_T L integral E plus M_T B t epsilon; bound t≤T and apply Gronwall. Requires ordinary continuous mild solutions / well-defined Bochner integrals.

records.title: State dependent killing as survival
records.label: thm:killing_survival
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[State dependent killing as survival]\label{thm:killing_survival}
Let \(Q\) be a finite Markov generator, let \(V\geq0\), and set
\[
A=Q-D_V.
\]
For an initial distribution \(p_0\), define
\[
S_V(t)=\one^T\e^{tA}p_0.
\]
Then
\[
S_V(t)
=
\Exp_{p_0}
\left[
\exp\left(
-\int_0^tV(X_s)\dd s
\right)
\right].
\]
Also,
\[
-S_V'(t)
=
\one^TD_V\e^{tA}p_0.
\]
The matrix \(A=Q-D_V\) has nonnegative off diagonal entries and nonpositive column sums, so it is the subgenerator of the transient killed chain. Thus the potential in the finite Feynman Kac formula is exactly a state dependent killing rate in the forward transient semigroup.
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Average \cref{thm:continuous_feynman_kac} with terminal function \(f=\one\) against the initial distribution. Transposition gives
\[
p_0^T\e^{t(Q^T-D_V)}\one
=
\one^T\e^{t(Q-D_V)}p_0.
\]
Since \(\one^TQ=0\), differentiation gives
\[
S_V'(t)
=
-\one^TD_V\e^{tA}p_0.
\]
\end{proof}

records.review_note: Transpose backward expectation then differentiate mass. Arbitrary V≥0 yields a substochastic killed chain, not necessarily transient or eventually absorbed; V=0 is boundary counterexample to wording.

records.title: Survival and hazard identities
records.label: thm:survival_hazard
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Survival and hazard identities]\label{thm:survival_hazard}
The event density and hazard are
\[
f(t)=a^T\e^{tA}p_0=-S'(t),
\qquad
h(t)=\frac{f(t)}{S(t)}
\]
whenever \(S(t)>0\). The survival function is nonincreasing and
\[
S(t)
=
\exp\left(
-\int_0^th(s)\dd s
\right).
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Because \(A\) is a Metzler matrix, \(\e^{tA}\) is nonnegative. The column sum assumption makes \(a^T\) nonnegative. Differentiate \(S(t)\):
\[
S'(t)=\one^TA\e^{tA}p_0=-a^T\e^{tA}p_0.
\]
The remaining identity follows by integrating \((\log S)'=-h\).
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Metzler positivity and nonpositive column sums yield nonnegative density and nonincreasing survival. A finite conservative survivor can have nonzero limiting mass; proper absorption is not automatic.

records.title: Laplace transform and moments
records.label: thm:survival_moments
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Laplace transform and moments]\label{thm:survival_moments}
Assume the spectrum of \(A\) lies in the open left half plane. Then absorption occurs with probability one. For \(s\geq0\),
\[
\Exp[\e^{-s\tau}]
=
a^T(sI-A)^{-1}p_0.
\] For every integer \(m\geq1\),
\[
\Exp[\tau^m]
=
m!\one^T(-A)^{-m}p_0.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
The Laplace transform follows by integrating the density in \cref{thm:survival_hazard}. Stability of \(A\) gives
\[
\int_0^\infty
\e^{-st}\e^{tA}\dd t
=
(sI-A)^{-1}.
\]
At \(s=0\),
\[
a^T(-A)^{-1}p_0
=
\one^Tp_0=1.
\]
For the moments,
\[
\int_0^\infty t^m\e^{tA}\dd t
=
m!(-A)^{-m-1}.
\]
Multiplying by \(a^T=\one^T(-A)\) gives the result. These are the standard matrix formulas for phase type laws \cite{Neuts1981,AsmussenNermanOlsson1996}.
\end{proof}
records.review_note: Explicit strict spectral stability ensures integrability and mass one. a^T=1^T(-A) cancels one inverse power, giving m!1^T(-A)^−m p0.

records.title: Residual life as a restarted semigroup
records.label: prop:residual_life
records.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Residual life as a restarted semigroup]\label{prop:residual_life}
For \(S(t)>0\), define the conditional transient distribution
\[
p_t
=
\frac{\e^{tA}p_0}{S(t)}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{S(t+s)}{S(t)}
=
\one^T\e^{sA}p_t.
\]
\end{proposition}
records.review_note: Divide positive surviving mass; semigroup law gives restarted conditional law. No memorylessness of scalar survival is inferred.

records.title: Competing risk packets
records.label: thm:competing_risks
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Competing risk packets]\label{thm:competing_risks}
Suppose the exit row splits into nonnegative cause rows
\[
a^T
=
\sum_{r=1}^q a_r^T.
\]
Define
\[
f_r(t)=a_r^T\e^{tA}p_0.
\]
Then
\[
f(t)=\sum_{r=1}^qf_r(t).
\]
The cause specific hazard is
\[
h_r(t)=\frac{f_r(t)}{S(t)},
\]
and
\[
h(t)=\sum_{r=1}^qh_r(t).
\]
The eventual probability of cause \(r\) is
\[
\int_0^\infty f_r(t)\dd t
=
a_r^T(-A)^{-1}p_0.
\]
\end{theorem}
